questions.q: How does the summary define emotional intelligence?
a: Awareness of your own and others' feelings, used to guide behavior
The ability to suppress emotions while at work
A high score on a standard intelligence test
The skill of persuading people to agree with you
questions.why: Lesson 1 defines it as awareness of feelings in yourself and others, used to shape your thoughts and actions.

questions.q: Which five elements does Goleman say make up emotional intelligence?
a: Self-awareness, self-regulation, motivation, empathy, social skills
Focus, discipline, patience, optimism, charisma
Planning, delegation, feedback, hiring, firing
Listening, speaking, writing, reading, numeracy
questions.why: Lesson 1 lists those five components and connects each one to performance at work.

questions.q: How does meditation build emotional intelligence, per the summary?
a: It trains your attention, which strengthens self-awareness
It removes all negative emotions permanently
It replaces the need for sleep and rest
It makes you more competitive with colleagues
questions.why: Lesson 2 says attention can be trained like a muscle, and that mastery of attention deepens self-knowledge.

questions.q: Why is self-awareness so important, according to the summary?
a: It activates the rational brain so choices beat impulses
It makes you less aware of other people's moods
It allows you to ignore your feelings entirely
It guarantees that you will be promoted quickly
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that self-awareness engages the neocortex, so behavior comes from conscious choice rather than impulse.

questions.q: What are the three sources of work-related happiness?
a: Pleasure, passion, and a sense of purpose
Salary, status, and job security
Freedom, variety, and competition
Praise, promotion, and vacation time
questions.why: Lesson 3 draws on Tony Hsieh's view that pleasure is brief, passion is sustainable and purpose is the most reliable.
